drivers_up: France has reported 7 locally acquired cases in 2026, indicating active transmission.

drivers_down: Historically, EU/EEA countries have rarely reported locally acquired chikungunya cases.
No other EU/EEA country besides France has reported cases in 2026 so far.
Public health measures and surveillance in Europe can quickly control outbreaks.
samples.why_might_be_wrong: Unexpected environmental changes or lapses in public health measures could increase the spread beyond current expectations.
samples.rationale: The historical base rate for locally acquired chikungunya in EU/EEA countries is low. As of August 2026, only France has reported cases, indicating limited spread so far. Active transmission in France suggests a potential for cases in nearby regions, but robust European public health systems and climate variability make broader outbreaks less certain. Given these factors, the most probable outcome is that 1 country will report cases by the end of 2026.
